answer_1.quote: To further evaluate the generalizability of SCULPT, we assess its performance on an open-ended generation task in comparison to OPRO and ProTeGi, using GPT-4o as the underlying model. Open-ended tasks typically involve higher ambiguity and demand a nuanced understanding of contextual dependencies to produce high-quality outputs. For this preliminary analysis, we selected the CNN/DailyMail summarization dataset (CNN Sum), where the objective is to generate concise summaries of news articles.
answer_1.outputs: summaries of news articles, multilabel classifications

answer_2.quote: Evaluation metrics included ROUGE-1 (R-1), ROUGE-2 (R-2), ROUGE-L (R-L), Cosine Similarity (Cos Sim) computed using a MiniLM sentence transformer, and their Harmonic Mean (HM) as an aggregate measure of performance.

answer_3.quote: Since sentence transformers cannot compare full-length prompts effectively, we employ GPT-4o (cf Appendix N) to assess prompt differences at the document level, accounting for logical restructuring, reordering, and coherence beyond surface-level semantic shifts.
